request.title: The Dog Who Never Stopped Waiting (Part 3/3)
request.description:
A statue while he was still alive, and a reunion 80 years in the making. Did Hachiko's ending get you?

Part 3 of 3: The Dog Who Never Stopped Waiting

extra_params.video_script: Hachiko got to see his own statue. In Part 2, a newspaper story made the waiting dog famous across Japan. In April 1934, a bronze statue of Hachiko was unveiled at Shibuya Station, and Hachiko was there. Less than a year later, he died. He had kept coming back for almost ten years. His ashes were buried in the same cemetery as Ueno. And in 2015, the University of Tokyo unveiled a new statue: Hachiko leaping up to greet his owner, together again at last.
